# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 113 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 52-53 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_113_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 113

**1** His disciples said to him: "When will the kingdom come?"

**2** Jesus said: "It will not come by watching for it. It will not be said: 'Look, here!' or 'Look, there!'

**3** Rather, the kingdom of the Father is spread out upon the earth, and people do not see it."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** Thomas's kingdom-timing saying (cf. Luke 17:20-21) is one of the most important in the entire gospel. Three critical points: (1) The kingdom does not come through observation (*parateresis*) — it is not a visible, dateable event. (2) It cannot be located ("here" or "there") — it has no geographic center. (3) It is already spread out upon the earth — the kingdom is present and omnipresent; the problem is human blindness, not divine delay.

**"Spread out upon the earth"** — *poh hijm pkah*: Thomas's unique formulation. Luke 17:21 says "within/among you" (*entos humon*); Thomas externalizes this to the cosmos.

**"People do not see it"** — the conclusion is one of the most haunting in Thomas. The kingdom is here; the human failure is perceptual. PNEUMA's "already" is an interpretive addition; SOPHIA does not add it, but the present-tense "is spread out" carries the same force.

**Synoptic Parallels:** Luke 17:20-21. Thomas's version extends the Lukan saying to include the cosmic "spread out upon the earth" and the blinding conclusion "people do not see it."
